settings.title: How your business is measured
settings.name: What this workspace is called
settings.timeExplains: Everything the product measures — how long something waited, whether it is late, when to chase — is counted against these. A wrong value here produces no error, only numbers that are quietly wrong.
settings.atRiskWindow: Hours before a deadline when work starts being flagged
settings.escalationHint: In order, longest last — for example 24, 72, 168. Each step waits longer than the one before it.
settings.quietHoursExplains: Nobody is chased between these times. A range that runs past midnight — from 22:00 to 06:00 — is the ordinary one and is exactly what you want.
settings.approvalRequired: A manager's invitation waits for my approval
settings.approvalExplains: With this off, a manager can invite somebody without asking you. Turning it off is giving away that decision, which is why only you can change it and why the change is recorded.
settings.appliesFromNow: Changes apply from now. Anything already measured keeps the values that were in force when it happened.
settings.nothingChanged: Nothing changed, so nothing was recorded.

error.heading: We could not open your settings
error.body: Something went wrong reading how your business is measured. Try again in a moment.
error.ladderUnordered: Each chase must wait longer than the one before it. Put the hours in order, smallest first.
error.atRiskWindow: The flagging window must be more than zero hours. At zero, everything is flagged, which is the same as nothing being flagged.
error.quietHoursCoverTheDay: Quiet hours cannot cover the whole day, or nobody would ever be chased.
error.noWorkingDays: Choose at least one working day, or nothing can be measured.
error.timezone: That is not a time zone we recognise.
error.couldNotSave: We could not save your settings. Nothing has changed.

settings.analysisExplains: These decide how the product judges your own history. They change what it says, never what it does.
settings.closureCoverageHint: When less than this share of the work behind a finding actually finished, the finding says so. Work that stalls is not a random sample, so a figure that quietly leaves it out reads as good news.
settings.idleWindowHint: How long a template goes unused before it is offered for retirement. Templates used on a regular rhythm are judged against that rhythm instead.
settings.approvalNotYet: Only you can invite people at the moment, so this has nothing to govern yet. When managers can invite, this decides whether their invitations wait for you.

organisation.title: Departments and jobs
organisation.lede: The parts this business has, the jobs inside them, and who holds which. A job is what a piece of marked work takes its kind from, so this list is the vocabulary the whole product reads work through.
organisation.failed: The organisation could not be read.
organisation.addJob: Add a job to this department
organisation.noJobs: No jobs here yet. A department with none records nothing about anybody's work.
organisation.emptyDescription: Add the parts this business is made of, then the jobs inside them.
organisation.whoLede: Work somebody marks takes its kind from the job they hold. Somebody with none recorded is an ordinary state — their work simply carries no kind until it is.

board.analysersLede: Small analysers over one snapshot. Each reads one component, answers one question, and says what it found, what it could not see, or that it looked and everything is fine.
board.coldStartLede: A run reads and records; it writes nothing into your libraries. This turns what it found into a task template for each kind of work and a process for each shape, as drafts you can read and change. Only finished engagements count — work in an engagement nobody closed is left out.
board.coverageAlt: {{read}} of {{total}} pieces of work in the window were read
board.decidedNote: An analyser that found nothing is not a failure. The row above says what each one read before it decided.
board.detectorNote: Grouped by the question each analyser was answering, in the order the stages depend on one another. A stage the run never reached is left out rather than drawn as a zero.
board.eachStageReads: Each stage reads the one before it
board.effortBasis: Effort figures — how long work took, what stalled, what came back — are measured over {{pieces}} pieces of work, not over the {{read}} marks above. A duration belongs to a piece of work, and one piece of work carries several marks.
board.foundThis_one: Found {{count}} thing worth deciding about, across {{read}} read.
board.foundThis_other: Found {{count}} things worth deciding about, across {{read}} read.
board.gateEyebrow: Do these and the pipeline starts working
board.gateHeadline_one: One missing thing is holding an analyser shut.
board.gateHeadline_other: {{count}} analysers are held shut by something that does not exist yet.
board.inspectorIdle: Pick an analyser and what it read, found and could not see appears here.
board.signatureMeaning: A fingerprint of what this run read. Two runs sharing it read exactly the same work.
board.lookedAndFine_one: Looked at {{count}} thing and found nothing wrong.
board.lookedAndFine_other: Looked at {{count}} things and found nothing wrong.
board.noEffortBasis: No effort figures on this page: the analyser that measures duration did not run.
board.noFindingsYet: No findings from the last run.
board.nothingUnseen: It reported no blind spot on this run.
board.runOnePass: Run one pass on its own
board.shapesNote: Nothing here has been written down. A shape becomes a process when somebody says so.
board.silenceEyebrow: Read and not acted on · this is normal
board.sourcesFailed: The engagements behind this could not be read.
board.sourcesLoading: Reading the engagements this was found in…
board.sourcesNone: This decision names its subject directly, so it rests on no separate rows.

stageQuestion.observe: What is there to look at?
stageQuestion.normalise: What is the shape of it?

board.teachAmber: Amber means blocked — it needs something that does not exist yet, and says exactly what.
board.teachGreen: Green means it produced a finding you can act on. Those queue up in Findings.
board.teachGrey: Grey means it ran and found nothing. That is an answer, not a failure.
board.threePasses: Three passes in the order their results feed each other. Nothing is written to your libraries.
board.writeItDown: Write down what the pipeline found

stage.foot: These are the run’s own ledger rows, not a summary of them. The reason is the word the pipeline wrote.

why.jobBoundary: A job boundary is a container rather than work, so it is not clustered or matched.
why.noSignal: The mark carried no words the clusterer could read.
why.noWorkType: Nobody recorded what kind of work this was, so it could not be keyed on one.
why.noEligibleTemplate: No approved template was substantial enough, or old enough, to be matched against this work.
why.textFloor: The words agreed too weakly with any template. This veto is absolute and is checked before the score.
why.belowFloor: Something matched, but not well enough to act on.
why.lowConfidence: The match was good but the evidence behind it was thin.
